asr.full_text: Welcome to Abhishek Shukl. Today, Abhishek with his IPS officer on duty. When he's on duty, he is very intense. When he's at home, he's as lively and natural at the same time. He inspires many people to join him on his duty. You know who this is and what he does today. When he has done everything at the duty, you are as ordinary person as a youth. She is a great impression. You are known as Amyooti too. Where did you begin and just where did you learn about your studies? My roots are in Durga, Chhattisgarh. We are three sisters. I have completed my studies in Durga. I finished my post graduation in Billahi. Did you think of doing UPSC or was it your ultimate goal in the beginning? When in the childhood, when we ask a child what do you wish to become when you grow up and my mom would usually tell us is that to become a doctor or engineer or something similar. In childhood when one asks this question to a child, he or she says Doctor, Engineer or something else. So that was the very same question my mother used to ask to me when I was young. I used to say that someone has to make me a grown up Kiranvedi. So it must have come in mind somewhere or the other. And then when my schooling came to an end in 11-12 so I started to have a stronger view about my work. I saw that I was in a business background In the year 2017, when schooling was about to end and my financial situation was going to change I had a commerce background, so my friends who were doing charter accounts... my Sir asked me why I was not applying for a CA So I said that I would be interested in civil services From then on my mind was at a standstill and I started getting ready for began preparations for it post graduation What was the environment in your house? You are three sisters You have different outlook towards the middle class family but one has thought that you will be a big person So you are planning to find a job for yourself if the most happened one would have to marry Did you even get the support from home? I must add that I was lucky We were three sisters and the whole family treated me like a tomboy When I grew up with my brothers All the activities were done by boys I was boy-cut almost till my 12 th There is a story, like the Bud was about me and Vivekananda from Booratalap I was on a walk with my brother in the morning 3 people were there, I crossed only twice While leaving they asked me Do you play the male role or the female one? I thought it was the male role I had dressed like a female character I just said, look at the slippers And then I left From top I looked like a boy. I wore slippers of boy's so I said look their slippers so i left from there. I grown up like that so same atmosphere I had in my school. What was you personality in your school from the start? Was there a big personality? Like what you see in this field now like what one has to face people. Was there a kind of personality from the beginning or was it different? No, no, it was like a change. Almost that I would find it in the genes. As I see from home, no such thing has happened but in every age you get a new thing. You get the truth, wrong and law of all these three things and can keep your words with a great perspective you are telling me about three sisters how your parents raised your sisters? when you have only girls in the family you feel they need a better boys is there any distinction like that? have you ever heard or seen among your relatives? What is the best thing that a right person should do if he or she is the son of a better mother. I have never heard anyone ask my father or mother to have a adopted child . They asked me to be like my own son. So it is always the other father's fault that keeps the grew up doing that. He still says daughter is better in this regard. So, there are no gaps. How did you start your journey? You had your education and schooling. And then you started planning UPSC. What made you think to start with UPSC, and for what reasons did you decide you got in? Let me tell you one thing. Because all those who may be listening to me, I had supplementary in 5th standard because I didn't understand Maths. I got only 5 marks in 50th standard. So it happens that it's not necessary. Sometimes it happens that we start to teach our children that it's not good to study. But we don't have to do this. We have to motivate them. Because in normal days your child will look golden. Maybe he is not performing well in academics. This means that he has a brain. Even if he is not showing it there, if he gets the right atmosphere, the right subject, the subject of his choice, then he will definitely outperform. I will definitely ask you to follow the youth. On small things, youths are in depression. Some even commit suicide looking at their failure. So, failure opens the way for success. Ankita Sharmaji is here. How did you come up with the idea of civil service? Where do you want to do it? How do you want to do it? Did you want to become an IPS? Or did you also think of IAS or something else? I was selected in my third attempt. In my first attempt, I put IPS in the first priority. I was second in IAS. Then I gave the mains, but I was not selected. Then in the second time, I was IPS in the first priority and second was IS. Then I gave the mains but I was not selected. Then in the second time, I was not cleared from the prelims and when I gave it in the third time, then my IS was the first option and IPS was the second option. And when I was doing post graduation, I understood that I should now get ready for this because after my graduation, almost my subject degree has ended. So then I started my self study in my house. After that I went to Delhi in October. I stayed there for six to seven months. Then I felt that my time is getting wasted a little. Because you have to manage a lot of things yourself. So I came back home and then I did self preparation. This is another thing to think about. UPSC has cleared did my self preparation. This is also something that should be thought through. They have cleared the UPSC exam with self preparation. They took a guide from Delhi for 6-7 months. In the meantime, you got married while preparing for the exam. Did you feel that your dream or goal was changing? Frankly, I have never felt that my dream is changing. Because it is my arranged marriage. Even when my husband came to meet me, I never thought that my dream is changing because it's my arranged marriage when my husband came to meet me then also I said that this is my dream and I want to do this so he said that don't worry, whatever you want to do so I was completely set in my mind that I have to do this and I will never left, right yes because we got married and after that he is in the army so it's a job with a lot of postings and transfers so he got transferred in 7-8 places Usually, women have careers but they change after marriage or leave it. What support should women get to achieve their goals in future after marriage? What kind of environment should they get? I would like to say two things in this. Firstly, both men and women should have self-confidence. I had two suggestions. First, each woman should believe in her dreams first and foremost. And the wife should believe in her dreams first and foremost. She should know that you can do something and you can do this. Until the time you don't show confidence in yourself, nobody can. As you move forward in your marriage, You can see of in-laws Because in any big dream, you need to be psychologically and mentally calm So the peace that you have, only your in-laws and family members can give you So you should support as much as possible Because the atmosphere nowadays is that Whether it is a boy or a girl, parents don't make any difference So they raise that daughter in such a way. So those who get married and go, they should understand how that girl has been raised. And they should try to create the same atmosphere for her so that she can achieve her dreams. You said a very important thing that the same atmosphere should be created in the in-laws as well. This is a very good! Ankita ji is there any pressure after marriage that after we have married we need to attain success Because when we are in our homes we also become failures. We allow our parents to accept and then give it to them. It's possible that we are not given the opportunities in such a way Because whenever you get married you create a time-boundation somewhere like I am married today We always see both success and loss But after there is failure, i used to feel I will not be able to use my family, and make money But then I used to make this decision In the beginning, I have thought of myself That i will make my dream come true My time limit has become fixed But i am feeling a psychological barrier in my mind But I think overcoming it is the first step to achieve your dream after marriage So how did you spend your time to study? It was very tough at that time The exam is for 8-9 months and the procedure is the same If the prelims are in June, then in October, November and December, the mains are done Then in April, the procedure is followed if there is a prelim in June, then in October-December there is a mains, then in April there is an interview so like the common people, I didn't have time to study for the whole year because I had a lot of work to do due to living at home and as I told you, there is a transfer job, so I had to settle here and there and go out, so I couldn't study at that time but when the exam came, suppose if there is a prelim exam in May so 2 months before was not able to study. But when the exams started, suppose that prillims exams are held in May, then two months before it, in the same way that I had to cover the whole year's exam. And those were the two months in which I was studying. That's when I didn't watch anything, day and night. When I would wake up, in the morning I would study in the same way that I read in the night too for as long as possible. Because you aren't writing this exam, alone. There were other people with you who had prepared for the whole year and they are writing it. So they are reading it according to their own needs for 8 hours, 6 hours, 10 hours in a day. You have to cover that 24 hours per day for 2 months. So I used to plan my strategy and study in that way. We heard that in the interview your poetry impressed the board a lot. Yes. What was the poetry? Do you write poems as well? Yes, it's my hobby. I write many poems. There was a poem in the book, Na koi band tujhe rok pae. I've recited it. Perhaps they will be happy. So, can you remember the story of this poem? In my preparation, I remember one day, I'm telling you, When you think about your time limit in the mind. When you think that your time limit is limitless, you want to do this but your family is waiting for you, Sheer de Himalay ke choti, ganga ke woh dhar ban Kar de Khakh raha ki yaad ko, tu kar apni jwala aisi bulan Kabhi tez, kabhi madham, kabhi ho saral Chahe jo ho teri raftar, bas barta chal You have written a very nice poem You have said that you will remember this poem when you fight What is your personality as an bit different from a police officer who is a hardworking cop who is always filled with a strong heart. I think that the image of the police, the portrait of the police, is like he is just an upright person. But, they rarely come to the fore behind the person. But, I think that, in all rank and file, from constable to the highest rank, everyone has that personality personality, soft corner. If we see a policemen from a close angle we will get to know of the softness that happens there. Please try to see a policeman with his children, you may feel like every policeman has soft corner and a soft person. When you got the first posting when what was going on in your mind when you received your first posting? What you had to do there? What were you thinking? When I was given for the first time by our DGP of this district and when I got it for the first time that I have got Balodabazar district I was very happy because our SP madam is here and she has a lot of name of her own in our state. She is one of the best IPS officers. I was very happy Many different kind of people come in this situation, how do you deal with that? As I have said earlier I deal with any such situation But first of all I try to make everyone understands what I am talking about And if they do not understand or don't know about it then I have to explain them in the least of way If they still haven't understood it then I need to explain them at the end First of all I try very carefully to explain it's not like that But it's and nothing special. You are on zero tolerance. We are hearing and some people are telling that you don't hesitate to take a strict step if something is going wrong. So, don't you hesitate in your first posting that there will be some controversy or something will go wrong? You are also considered as a youth icon in Chhattisgarh. Your work is not only in the district but also in the entire region. People see you in the state. Especially on YouTube, I have seen that your videos are included with many inspirational songs. How do you feel after getting success and coming to this job? When you are praised for your work? First of all, when you talk about YouTube, sometimes I do any wrong thing, they themselves step back from doing it. And if they see that my officer is taking a stand for me, for the truth, then they themselves start taking a stand for the truth. And automatically, an atmosphere like this is created in the entire service. Sir, I have two questions. Firstly, you got a female officer when you joined, so you must have got some benefit from this. And the second question is, there is a male mentality, that if a lady is leading you, then there is a slight hesitation or you cannot accept the old mentality. Did you get to see any such thing? First of all, it is a question from the lady officer. When our DGP sir allotted me under Madam Many people told me that maybe I should have allotted you because you are a lady and Madam is also a lady But now I feel that was the best decision and the turning point of my career That I should get a mam And something like that, as you asked the second question So something like that is in question, the subordinates have this in their minds, I have not yet found that they have this in their minds that you can do this. Moreover, it happens that if you see my performance of these many days, for one month, two months, whatever the performance must have been, then they also gradually understand that what kind of an officer I am. Will we see him as a woman or as an officer? So this is their own decision. How did you get the opportunity to lead the parade? Because many people were impressed by your lead. Again, my seniors chose that opportunity. That I should lead the 26th January parade which was led by the Governor. I found that a very good opportunity. Because it was a bit historical that till today no women IPS has ever led a parade and it was the first time in our 19 years when our state was formed that a female officer has led and it was a very proud moment and I was very happy and it always used to happen that on 26th January I used to watch the Delhi parade so I was very attached to the parade Even in the army, they don't get much leave. We thought that we don't get much leave. But we try to coordinate their leave and when we meet them, they come here to meet me. Then we meet each other. I haven't planned much, I'm still focusing on this. So that's it. We try to do that. IPAs have been formed. What response do you have from your family? I am trying to focus on that only. That's all I am trying to do. You have become an IPS. What is the response of your family, friends, friends, and relatives? They feel very proud because there is no one in my family who serves me like this. They feel proud. And when they see the right thing, you show the right thing in media through media. When they see the right thing, they feel feel proud of me for doing the right thing. or I am honestly fulfilling my work. What have you thought of in the future? How do you want to progress your career? Are there any other targets in your mind? Because you have already completed one target. Yes, now I feel I am in the infancy of my service. I am very young to say anything. I am a grown grown up in service. It's only been 2 months and I'm 30 years out of service. I haven't thought of opening myself up and doing the work as per the demand. But I have one goal always, that I work in the area for women, society and police? You said three things, women's contribution, police's contribution and society's contribution. So the first question is the most accurate, that women's contribution. As I said, every woman should have faith in herself. Now, like there are small women, who are bringing themselves up through social media. Those are women who are making their career. Even my mother was a woman who awakened this dream inside me that I dream of becoming like Kiran Bedi. So first you have to believe in yourself and your rights. You should know your rights. Unless you know your rights, you can't fight for them. And as I said in the society, they should give you the right atmosphere. And I am very happy to see that. When I see that my security guards tell me that the photo you have given me is not right. in our police station, which is called the Temple of Justice If someone comes there and we have some problem, then first of all we should listen to them In the easiest way, for that which is best for them we should try to provide them that support Often times, it happens that only through words if we listen to them carefully and explain it to their family members then many problems get solved I think when we are in police stations, I see that 40-50% of cases are related to women We made it so that the children can drink water there. There are small things that you can establish a connection with the society and make a connection that the police is something else than just this uniform. We had with us Lady Dabang IPS Officer Ankita Sharma, who talked to us and found out that there is a woman behind Kh deals with criminals with great power. She writes poems. She has struggled a lot to get this status. I hope that her story which has come in Bansal News will inspire youths and they will learn a lot. Especially women. That's all for now. See you next time with another person. Till then, goodbye.

Did you want to become an IPS? Or did you also think of IAS or something else? I was selected in my third attempt. In my first attempt, I put IPS in the first priority. I was second in IAS. Then I gave the mains, but I was not selected. Then in the second time, I was IPS in the first priority and second was IS. Then I gave the mains but I was not selected. Then in the second time, I was not cleared from the prelims and when I gave it in the third time, then my IS was the first option and IPS was the second option. And when I was doing post graduation, I understood that I should now get ready for this because after my graduation, almost my subject degree has ended. So then I started my self study in my house. After that I went to Delhi in October. I stayed there for six to seven months. Then I felt that my time is getting wasted a little. Because you have to manage a lot of things yourself. So I came back home and then I did self preparation. This is another thing to think about. UPSC has cleared did my self preparation. This is also something that should be thought through. They have cleared the UPSC exam with self preparation. They took a guide from Delhi for 6-7 months. In the meantime, you got married while preparing for the exam. Did you feel that your dream or goal was changing? Frankly, I have never felt that my dream is changing. Because it is my arranged marriage. Even when my husband

came to meet me, I never thought that my dream is changing because it's my arranged marriage when my husband came to meet me then also I said that this is my dream and I want to do this so he said that don't worry, whatever you want to do so I was completely set in my mind that I have to do this and I will never left, right yes because we got married and after that he is in the army so it's a job with a lot of postings and transfers so he got transferred in 7-8 places Usually, women have careers but they change after marriage or leave it. What support should women get to achieve their goals in future after marriage? What kind of environment should they get? I would like to say two things in this. Firstly, both men and women should have self-confidence. I had two suggestions. First, each woman should believe in her dreams first and foremost. And the wife should believe in her dreams first and foremost. She should know that you can do something and you can do this. Until the time you don't show confidence in yourself, nobody can. As you move forward in your marriage, You can see of in-laws Because in any big dream, you need to be psychologically and mentally calm So the peace that you have, only your in-laws and family members can give you So you should support as much as possible Because the atmosphere nowadays is that Whether it is a boy or a girl, parents don't make any difference So they raise that daughter in such a way. So those who get married and go, they should understand how that girl has been raised. And they should try to create the same atmosphere for her so

that she can achieve her dreams. You said a very important thing that the same atmosphere should be created in the in-laws as well. This is a very good! Ankita ji is there any pressure after marriage that after we have married we need to attain success Because when we are in our homes we also become failures. We allow our parents to accept and then give it to them. It's possible that we are not given the opportunities in such a way Because whenever you get married you create a time-boundation somewhere like I am married today We always see both success and loss But after there is failure, i used to feel I will not be able to use my family, and make money But then I used to make this decision In the beginning, I have thought of myself That i will make my dream come true My time limit has become fixed But i am feeling a psychological barrier in my mind But I think overcoming it is the first step to achieve your dream after marriage So how did you spend your time to study? It was very tough at that time The exam is for 8-9 months and the procedure is the same If the prelims are in June, then in October, November and December, the mains are done Then in April, the procedure is followed if there is a prelim in June, then in October-December there is a mains, then in April there is an interview so like the common people, I didn't have time to study for the whole year because I had a lot of work to do due to living at home and as I told you, there is a transfer job, so I had to settle here and there and go out, so I couldn't study at that time but when the exam came, suppose if

there is a prelim exam in May so 2 months before was not able to study. But when the exams started, suppose that prillims exams are held in May, then two months before it, in the same way that I had to cover the whole year's exam. And those were the two months in which I was studying. That's when I didn't watch anything, day and night. When I would wake up, in the morning I would study in the same way that I read in the night too for as long as possible. Because you aren't writing this exam, alone. There were other people with you who had prepared for the whole year and they are writing it. So they are reading it according to their own needs for 8 hours, 6 hours, 10 hours in a day. You have to cover that 24 hours per day for 2 months. So I used to plan my strategy and study in that way. We heard that in the interview your poetry impressed the board a lot. Yes. What was the poetry? Do you write poems as well? Yes, it's my hobby. I write many poems. There was a poem in the book, Na koi band tujhe rok pae. I've recited it. Perhaps they will be happy. So, can you remember the story of this poem? In my preparation, I remember one day, I'm telling you, When you think about your time limit in the mind. When you think that your time limit is limitless, you want to do this but your family is waiting for you, Sheer de Himalay ke choti, ganga ke woh dhar ban Kar de Khakh raha ki yaad ko, tu kar apni jwala aisi bulan Kabhi tez, kabhi madham, kabhi ho saral Chahe jo ho teri raftar, bas barta chal You have written a very nice poem You have said that you will remember this poem when you

fight What is your personality as an bit different from a police officer who is a hardworking cop who is always filled with a strong heart. I think that the image of the police, the portrait of the police, is like he is just an upright person. But, they rarely come to the fore behind the person. But, I think that, in all rank and file, from constable to the highest rank, everyone has that personality personality, soft corner. If we see a policemen from a close angle we will get to know of the softness that happens there. Please try to see a policeman with his children, you may feel like every policeman has soft corner and a soft person. When you got the first posting when what was going on in your mind when you received your first posting? What you had to do there? What were you thinking? When I was given for the first time by our DGP of this district and when I got it for the first time that I have got Balodabazar district I was very happy because our SP madam is here and she has a lot of name of her own in our state. She is one of the best IPS officers. I was very happy Many different kind of people come in this situation, how do you deal with that? As I have said earlier I deal with any such situation But first of all I try to make everyone understands what I am talking about And if they do not understand or don't know about it then I have to explain them in the least of way If they still haven't understood it then I need to explain them at the end First of all I try very carefully to explain it's not like that But it's and nothing special. You are on zero tolerance.

We are hearing and some people are telling that you don't hesitate to take a strict step if something is going wrong. So, don't you hesitate in your first posting that there will be some controversy or something will go wrong? You are also considered as a youth icon in Chhattisgarh. Your work is not only in the district but also in the entire region. People see you in the state. Especially on YouTube, I have seen that your videos are included with many inspirational songs. How do you feel after getting success and coming to this job? When you are praised for your work? First of all, when you talk about YouTube, sometimes I do any wrong thing, they themselves step back from doing it. And if they see that my officer is taking a stand for me, for the truth, then they themselves start taking a stand for the truth. And automatically, an atmosphere like this is created in the entire service. Sir, I have two questions. Firstly, you got a female officer when you joined, so you must have got some benefit from this. And the second question is, there is a male mentality, that if a lady is leading you, then there is a slight hesitation or you cannot accept the old mentality. Did you get to see any such thing? First of all, it is a question from the lady officer. When our DGP sir allotted me under Madam Many people told me that maybe I should have allotted you because you are a lady and Madam is also a lady But now I feel that was the best decision and the turning point of my career That I should get a mam And something like that, as you asked the second question So something like

that is in question, the subordinates have this in their minds, I have not yet found that they have this in their minds that you can do this. Moreover, it happens that if you see my performance of these many days, for one month, two months, whatever the performance must have been, then they also gradually understand that what kind of an officer I am. Will we see him as a woman or as an officer? So this is their own decision. How did you get the opportunity to lead the parade? Because many people were impressed by your lead. Again, my seniors chose that opportunity. That I should lead the 26th January parade which was led by the Governor. I found that a very good opportunity. Because it was a bit historical that till today no women IPS has ever led a parade and it was the first time in our 19 years when our state was formed that a female officer has led and it was a very proud moment and I was very happy and it always used to happen that on 26th January I used to watch the Delhi parade so I was very attached to the parade Even in the army, they don't get much leave. We thought that we don't get much leave. But we try to coordinate their leave and when we meet them, they come here to meet me. Then we meet each other. I haven't planned much, I'm still focusing on this. So that's it. We try to do that. IPAs have been formed. What response do you have from your family? I am trying to focus on that only. That's all I am trying to do. You have become an IPS. What is the response of your family, friends, friends, and relatives? They feel very proud because there is no one in my

family who serves me like this. They feel proud. And when they see the right thing, you show the right thing in media through media. When they see the right thing, they feel feel proud of me for doing the right thing. or I am honestly fulfilling my work. What have you thought of in the future? How do you want to progress your career? Are there any other targets in your mind? Because you have already completed one target. Yes, now I feel I am in the infancy of my service. I am very young to say anything. I am a grown grown up in service. It's only been 2 months and I'm 30 years out of service. I haven't thought of opening myself up and doing the work as per the demand. But I have one goal always, that I work in the area for women, society and police? You said three things, women's contribution, police's contribution and society's contribution. So the first question is the most accurate, that women's contribution. As I said, every woman should have faith in herself. Now, like there are small women, who are bringing themselves up through social media. Those are women who are making their career. Even my mother was a woman who awakened this dream inside me that I dream of becoming like Kiran Bedi. So first you have to believe in yourself and your rights. You should know your rights. Unless you know your rights, you can't fight for them. And as I said in the society, they should give you the right atmosphere. And I am very happy to see that. When I see that my security guards tell me that the photo you have given me is not right. in our police station, which is called the

Temple of Justice If someone comes there and we have some problem, then first of all we should listen to them In the easiest way, for that which is best for them we should try to provide them that support Often times, it happens that only through words if we listen to them carefully and explain it to their family members then many problems get solved I think when we are in police stations, I see that 40-50% of cases are related to women We made it so that the children can drink water there. There are small things that you can establish a connection with the society and make a connection that the police is something else than just this uniform. We had with us Lady Dabang IPS Officer Ankita Sharma, who talked to us and found out that there is a woman behind Kh deals with criminals with great power. She writes poems. She has struggled a lot to get this status. I hope that her story which has come in Bansal News will inspire youths and they will learn a lot. Especially women. That's all for now. See you next time with another person. Till then, goodbye.
